approach: The speed of sound in the gas from the standing wave equals the speed from the adiabatic gas formula, since the node separation gives the wavelength.

steps.text: Write the speed of sound in a gas of adiabatic constant γ.
Relate the node separation to the wavelength. Successive nodes of a standing wave are half a wavelength apart.
Write the wave speed from the frequency and this wavelength.
Equate the two expressions for v and square both sides.

common_mistakes.text: Taking the node separation L itself as the full wavelength (forgetting nodes are half a wavelength apart), giving v = fL and γ = Mf²L²/RT.
Inverting the node-separation relation as L = 2λ instead of λ = 2L, giving λ = L/2, v = fL/2, and γ = Mf²L²/4RT.
